verdict: Second read agrees with the first: clean. Literal search finds no forbidden word or phrase, no em-dash, and both exclamation points inside John 20:28. 'In short' and 'truly' occur only inside verbatim quotations (Theodoret, Constantine). Two of six findings kept, both 'should'; four dropped as plain human prose or as replacements that were worse than the original. Nothing added.

keep.quote: That question matters to ordinary faith more than most people expect, and Constantine's first instinct, that this was a quarrel over words, sounds a good deal more like many American Christians than anything the bishops said.
keep.tell: Vague framing sentence; a comparison that does not parse (an instinct 'sounds like' Christians, then like 'anything the bishops said')
keep.replacement: That question matters to ordinary faith more than most people expect, and Constantine's first instinct, that this was a quarrel over words, is a good deal closer to what many American Christians think than anything the bishops said.
keep.note: First reader's replacement dropped 'first instinct', which the ledger (item 4a) protects: Constantine later pressed homoousios himself. This version keeps 'first instinct', 'quarrel over words', 'many American Christians' and 'anything the bishops said' exactly, and only repairs the comparison.

keep.quote: Some resisted *homoousios* because they feared it erased the difference between the Father and the Son. The history is messier than the Sunday school version.
keep.tell: Paragraph ends by restating itself as a slogan; stock phrase
keep.replacement: Some resisted *homoousios* because they feared it erased the difference between the Father and the Son.
keep.note: The paragraph has already shown the mess through Hanson; the section already has its one verdict line ('We shouldn't tell that part as a simple victory'). Cutting loses no fact.

dropped: 'And if anyone bent the gospel to fit Greek philosophy, Arius is at least as easy to accuse.' Dropped: a gap in the argument, not an AI tell, and the proposed fix adds a newly voiced objection ('People also say ...') the ledger does not carry. Passed to for_james instead.
'The tide turned with Theodosius.' Dropped: an ordinary idiom any person would use; 'Theodosius changed that.' has a vague 'that' and is no better.
'To them Arius sounds sensible. In the 320s plenty of bishops thought so too.' Dropped: the looseness is how a person talks, and the short pair lands the section. Not machine-sounding.

'Athanasius became bishop of Alexandria in 328. In 335 a council at Tyre deposed him, and Constantine sent him into exile at Trier, in Gaul.' Dropped: the replacement is an and-and run-on that reads worse; a short chronicle paragraph is right for a list of reversals.
for_james: The paragraph beginning 'And if anyone bent the gospel to fit Greek philosophy' answers a charge the Case Against Nicaea section never states. If you want it tied in, one sentence of yours in that section naming the Greek-philosophy charge would do it; we did not write one for you.
